newsitem.title: UK: Zeneca licenses CarboMed anti-cancer drug.
newsitem.headline: Zeneca licenses CarboMed anti-cancer drug.

text.p: British drugs and specialty chemicals company Zeneca Group Plc said on Monday it was to develop a potential new cancer drug licensed from privately-owned U.S.-research company CarboMed Inc.
In a statement, Zeneca said it had assumed all costs related to developing and commercialising the new drug, known as CM101, which had shown promise against solid cancer tumours in animal studies.
It said the drug was being developed for a broad range of uses providing long-term suppression of disease and prolonged survival.

Zeneca Pharmaceuticals development director Richard Auty said CM101 represented a "novel approach to a broad-spectrum anti-cancer agent. It therefore provides a significant opportunity for Zeneca to broaden its already strong development portfolio in the oncology area."
Under the agreement Zeneca has paid an unspecified initial amount to Tennessee-based CarboMed and will pay further milestones, plus royalties dependent on sales.
